J1_line_asserts_challenged_proposition.justification: The response challenges 'A continuous map of locales is a locale isomorphism if and only if it is the opposite of a frame homomorphism.' That is the biconditional at lines 14-17 ('By definition of locale isomorphism: / $f$ is a locale isomorphism / iff: / $f = h^{op}$ for some frame homomorphism'), and the parsed first choice, line 17, is its right-hand side and carries the operative words 'for some frame homomorphism'. Assumptions in force: P3-P4 (L_1, L_2 locales and f a continuous map of Loc), line 2 (Loc is the dual of Frm) and lines 4-12 (isomorphisms of Loc are exactly the opposites of frame isomorphisms). So the first choice does carry the challenged proposition.

J2_evidence_specified.justification: A concrete instance is named inside the general phrasing: 'Any continuous map of locales that is not an isomorphism (such as the map corresponding to the unique frame homomorphism from the two-element frame to the one-element frame) is the opposite of a frame homomorphism but is not a locale isomorphism.' The two frames and the map between them are pinned down uniquely, so there is something definite to check.

J3_evidence_check.justification: Model-assisted judgment, with the finite part computed in scripts/P27_check.py. The script confirms that the unique function from the two-element frame {0<1} to the one-element frame preserves finite meets, arbitrary joins (including the empty join, i.e. the bottom) and the top, so it is a frame homomorphism, and that it is not injective, hence not a frame isomorphism; the two frames have different cardinalities, so they are not isomorphic at all. Therefore f = h^op satisfies the right-hand side of lines 14-17 while the corresponding locales are not isomorphic, so f is not an isomorphism of locales: the biconditional fails in the direction right-to-left, exactly as the response says, and the missing word in line 17 is 'isomorphism' in place of 'homomorphism'. The one step that is a reading rather than a computation, stated rather than repaired: the packet contains no independent definition of 'locale isomorphism' (line 14-17 is itself the page's report of it), so I read the term with its standard meaning of an invertible map of locales, which is what the page's title and P6 presuppose; the internal evidence agrees, since lines 4-12 identify isomorphisms of Loc with opposites of frame isomorphisms, and line 19's 'The result follows' only goes through if line 17 said isomorphism. If instead line 17 were read as a stipulative definition, it could not be counterexampled at all and the false assertion would move to P6 or line 19.

J4_consequence_overreach.justification: The response emits only the ranked labels (17, 15, 14), the claim and the counterexample; it states no consequence, in particular nothing about the page's result P6 or about the cited lemmas at lines 4 and 9.

notes: The mathematics of the witness is trivial and machine-checkable (a non-injective frame homomorphism exists); the judgment rests on reading 'locale isomorphism' as an invertible map of locales rather than as whatever line 17 stipulates. A second reader should decide that reading explicitly, since on the stipulative reading the same page is still wrong but at P6/line 19 rather than at line 17. Also worth noting: the witness needs the one-element (degenerate) frame to count as a frame, which is standard but not stated in the packet.
